📖 How to use

  1. Type the integrand as a function of x, e.g. sin(x) + x^2.
  2. Enter the limits a and b and the number of subintervals n.
  3. Choose Simpson's, trapezoidal or midpoint rule and press Integrate.
  4. Read the estimate, the exact formula applied, and how the value converges as n grows.

❓ Frequently asked questions

Which rule is most accurate?

Simpson's rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3 and usually converges fastest (error ~ 1/n⁴). The tool shows all three side by side so you can compare.

Why must n be even for Simpson's rule?

Simpson's rule fits parabolas over pairs of subintervals, so it needs an even count. The tool rounds an odd n up and tells you.

What functions can I type?

Polynomials (x^2), sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, exp, ln, log (base 10), sqrt, abs, pi, e, and the usual + − * / ^ operators with parentheses.
